title: Anthropic Sets a $70 to $78 IPO Range for Up to 825 Million Shares; Trading Reported for Nov. 19
dek: An amended SEC filing sets a $70 to $78 range for Nasdaq ticker ANT. CNBC reported pricing on Nov. 18 and trading on Nov. 19; compute suppliers agreed to buy $26 billion at the IPO price.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: Digital billboard on the Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square, New York City

keyPoints: An amended registration statement filed with the SEC on Nov. 10 sets a price range of $70 to $78 per Class A share for 825 million shares, to be listed on Nasdaq as ANT, according to CNBC and Decrypt.
CNBC, citing people familiar with the details, reported that Anthropic plans to price on Nov. 18 and begin trading on Nov. 19. FinanceFeeds noted that the filing itself did not state a date.
At the top of the range, CNBC reported net proceeds of up to $64.35 billion.
Seven companies that supply Anthropic computing power agreed to buy a combined $26 billion of non-voting Class N stock at the IPO price, Decrypt reported, citing the filing.
body:
Anthropic has set the terms for its planned initial public offering, and the reported timetable puts the first trade on Nasdaq on Nov. 19. The AI lab filed an amended registration statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Tuesday, Nov. 10, setting a price range of $70 to $78 per Class A share for 825 million shares. The stock would trade under the ticker ANT.

## What the filing sets

CNBC reported net proceeds of up to $64.35 billion at the top of the range. Decrypt put the gross figure at about $64.4 billion, including shares sold by existing stockholders. Decrypt, reading the filing, said underwriters have an option to buy a further 123.75 million shares. The price range is the step before pricing, which sets the final per-share figure.

## The timetable is reported, not yet filed

CNBC reported, citing people familiar with the details who were not authorized to speak publicly, that Anthropic plans to price on Nov. 18 and trade on Nov. 19. A Decrypt report carried by Yahoo Finance repeated those dates and attributed them to CNBC's reporting. FinanceFeeds noted that the filing itself did not state a date. Treat the dates as reported timing until pricing is announced.

## Valuation and retail allocation

CNBC reported that at the top of the range the company could be worth up to $1.405 trillion on a fully diluted basis, up from the $965 billion valuation from its May funding round. Decrypt, using the share count in the filing, put the market value on a basic basis at roughly $916 billion to $1.02 trillion. CNBC also reported that Anthropic is targeting a retail allocation of about 20 percent, well above the 5 to 10 percent that is typical for IPOs.

Some investors have been preparing for a lower number. CNBC reported that shareholders said even $1.5 trillion is now in doubt, after Anthropic had been looking toward $2 trillion.

## Chipmakers and cloud suppliers buy in

Decrypt, citing the filing, reported that seven companies that supply Anthropic's computing power agreed to buy a combined $26 billion of Class N common stock at the IPO price in a private placement. Those companies are AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC. At the midpoint of the range, Google and Nvidia would each buy about $10 billion, according to Decrypt's reading of the filing. Those shares would not be subject to the usual post-IPO lock-up. Meridian has covered the earlier [Broadcom financing backstop](/article/broadcom-backstops-63-billion-anthropic-chip-financing) separately.

## Financials and governance

Decrypt, citing the amended filing, reported that Anthropic had $33.2 billion of revenue in the first nine months of 2026, up from $2.5 billion a year earlier. It also reported a net loss of $104 billion for the period, most of it from a $94.3 billion non-cash charge tied to convertible notes and other instruments, and an operating loss of $1.26 billion.

Anthropic will list as a public benefit corporation. Its Long-Term Benefit Trust will elect a majority of the board. A single Class F share, held by an entity owned by its seven co-founders, carries 50.1 percent of the company's voting power on most matters, Decrypt reported.

## Why it matters for AI infrastructure

For Nvidia and the other suppliers, the IPO is both a customer story and an investment. A successful debut would support demand for AI infrastructure. A weak one would give investors a new reason to question valuations across the sector. Nvidia's own leadership change, announced Nov. 12, adds to that uncertainty; see [our report on Jensen Huang's resignation](/article/nvidia-jensen-huang-resigns-colette-kress-interim-ceo).

## A note on China

Anthropic's own website describes a policy update that prohibits companies more than 50 percent owned, directly or indirectly, by entities in regions where its products are not permitted, such as China. Coverage from Tom's Hardware and NotebookCheck dates that policy update to early September 2025. Meridian did not find a reliable source for a new block that takes effect on Nov. 12, 2026, so this story does not report one.

marketImpact.summary: The filing ties several AI chip and cloud suppliers to Anthropic through a $26 billion private placement at the IPO price. A strong debut would support their AI-infrastructure demand narrative. A weak one, or further doubts about the valuation, would weigh on sentiment toward the same names. The dates are reported, not filed, so confidence is low.
marketImpact.timeframe: Nov. 17 to Nov. 19, around Nvidia results and the reported pricing and first trading day
